message.content:
Based on my search, here is comprehensive information about calcium-containing foods:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

Dairy products are the most concentrated and best-absorbed sources of calcium:

- **Yogurt, plain low-fat** (8 oz): 415 mg calcium
- **Milk, nonfat** (1 cup): 299 mg calcium
- **Milk, whole** (1 cup): 276-300 mg calcium
- **Mozzarella, part-skim** (1.5 oz): 333 mg calcium
- **Cheddar cheese** (1.5 oz shredded): 306 mg calcium
- **Cottage cheese, 1% fat** (1 cup): 138 mg calcium
- **Ricotta, part-skim** (1/2 cup): 337 mg calcium

## Fish with Edible Bones

- **Sardines, canned in oil with bones** (3 oz): 325 mg calcium
- **Salmon, pink, canned with bones** (3 oz): 181 mg calcium

## Fortified Foods

- **Calcium-fortified orange juice** (1 cup): 349 mg calcium
- **Soymilk, calcium-fortified** (1 cup): 299 mg calcium
- **Almond milk, fortified** (1 cup): 482 mg calcium
- **Breakfast cereals, fortified** (1 serving): 100-1,000 mg calcium (varies)
- **Tofu, firm, made with calcium sulfate** (1/2 cup): 253 mg calcium

## Leafy Green Vegetables

Note: Some greens contain oxalic acid which reduces calcium absorption, but others are excellent sources:

- **Collard greens, cooked** (1 cup): 324 mg calcium
- **Kale, cooked** (1 cup): 177-94 mg calcium (varies by preparation)
- **Bok choy (Chinese cabbage)**, raw shredded (1 cup): 74 mg calcium
- **Turnip greens, boiled** (1/2 cup): 99 mg calcium
- **Spinach** has high calcium but only ~5% absorption due to oxalic acid

## Legumes, Nuts, and Seeds

- **Soybeans, cooked** (1/2 cup): 131 mg calcium
- **Edamame, cooked** (1 cup): 130 mg calcium
- **Chia seeds** (1 tablespoon): 76 mg calcium
- **Almonds** (1 oz): 76 mg calcium
- **Sesame seeds/tahini** (1 tablespoon): 64 mg calcium

## Other Sources

- **Broccoli** (1/2 cup raw): 21 mg calcium
- **Dried figs** (4): 54 mg calcium
- **Oranges** (1 medium): 60-65 mg calcium
- **White bread** (1 slice): 31 mg calcium

## Important Notes

- Adults up to age 50 need about **1,000 mg calcium daily**; women over 50 and men over 70 need **1,200 mg daily**
- Calcium absorption from dairy and fortified foods is about **30%**
- Some plant foods (spinach, chard) contain compounds that bind calcium and reduce absorption
- Vitamin D is essential for proper calcium absorption

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
4. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
5. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
6. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
